newsItems.headline: Gold recovers from two-week low ahead of US inflation - Reuters

briefing.briefing: Right now, the two biggest forces shaping gold are a moderately firm US dollar (DXY around 101) paired with real yields [the interest rate after stripping out inflation, which makes holding gold less attractive when high] sitting at 2.32% — both of these act as headwinds for gold. However, geopolitical stress remains elevated (the GPR risk index is at 173.6, well above normal), which historically provides a floor under gold prices and keeps buyers interested on dips. The only notable headline in the last 24 hours came from Reuters about 6.5 hours ago, noting gold is recovering from a two-week low ahead of US inflation data — this tells us price recently dipped and is attempting to bounce, likely as traders position cautiously before a key data release. There is no US inflation print on today's calendar (the calendar shows no scheduled events today), but the headline strongly implies a CPI [Consumer Price Index, the main inflation report] release is coming very soon, probably tomorrow or later this week — and that kind of uncertainty typically keeps price choppy and range-bound in the lead-up. With gold already having used roughly 50 of its average 98-point daily range today, about half the expected daily move is already done, meaning the remaining runway for a big directional push today is limited. Positioning from large traders [the COT report, showing what big futures players hold] remains net-long but barely changed week-over-week, suggesting no strong new conviction in either direction — crowding is rated NEUTRAL. The directional bias leans very slightly bullish given the bounce off lows and geopolitical support, but confidence is low at 4/10 — if the upcoming inflation data comes in hotter than expected, the dollar could spike and gold could sell off hard, flipping this view bearish quickly. For a trend-following trader using ICT concepts: wait for the 1H chart to clearly confirm higher highs and higher lows before committing, use reduced position size given the data uncertainty ahead, and avoid chasing moves late in the London session when daily range is half-consumed. The golden rule for today: if you can't see a clear trend on the 1-hour chart AND you don't know what the inflation number will be, the safest trade is no trade.
